name: RecallWhy
tagline: Agents that tell a retailer which recalled products are on its shelves — and why they believe it.
track: Track 2: The Agent That Can Explain Why

agents.name: Scout
agents.role: Reads live CPSC and FDA recall feeds and the item master through Zetaris; one federated REST x JDBC UPC sweep; opens one case per recall that touches the catalog.

agents.name: Investigator
agents.role: Decides which candidate SKUs a recall covers (UPC/model rules, NVIDIA Nemotron judge for text matches, H-MEM prior decisions), reads lot codes, computes exposure with federated SQL.

agents.name: Auditor
agents.role: Can block. Re-checks UPCs against the live notice in Zetaris, checks quotes and lot codes are verbatim in the notice, re-derives every exposure number with its own SQL, rejects briefs that state unsupported numbers. Max 2 revision rounds, then escalates to a human queue.

agents.name: Briefer
agents.role: Writes the action brief only from the World Model context builder, citing evidence ids.

zetaris.how: All agent data access is Zetaris Lightning SQL over its REST API. Two live Lightning REST tables (saferproducts.gov CPSC recalls, a top-level JSON array; api.fda.gov food enforcement) flattened into schemastore views, and two JDBC datasources (synthetic ERP and supplier-portal Postgres databases). Agents run federated queries joining live REST feeds with JDBC tables and the two databases with each other; the Auditor re-queries Zetaris independently to verify numbers.

meterless.how: Two Meterless agent engines mounted from github.com/Meterless/Meterless (Apache-2.0 reference implementations): H-MEM stores every adjudication (agent, medium trust) and every human decision (high trust) and is read before each judgement; World Model holds recall, case and finding facts with provenance (which SQL, which agent, which model call), and its context builder is the only input the Briefer sees.

cursor.how: Repository developed in Cursor. The Cursor agent (CLI, Auto model) scaffolded the project, wrote the synthetic retailer generator and Postgres loader, the Zetaris REST runner and the DuckDB sample-mode runner with their tests; each change was reviewed and fixed before committing (see commit messages marked 'Cursor agent').

nvidia.how: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Nano (30B-A3B, via Ollama) is the default model behind the single injected generator: it judges text matches between a recall notice and an item-master line, reads lot codes out of messy code_info text, and writes the why-paragraph that the Auditor checks. Any OpenAI-compatible endpoint (NVIDIA API Catalog, Meterless runtime) can replace it via env vars.

live: CPSC SaferProducts Recall API (U.S. government, public domain)
openFDA food enforcement API (public domain, CC0 per open.fda.gov/license)
data.synthetic: Northwind Mercantile retailer: stores, item master, inventory lots, weekly sales, supplier ship notices — generated by scripts/gen-synthetic.ts (seeded). About 120 SKUs are deliberately derived from real recall notices so the catalog overlaps the feeds; ground truth for evaluation is kept in data/synthetic/eval/ and never read by the agents. No personal data.
data.sample_snapshots: sample/ holds feed snapshots captured on the date in sample/CAPTURED_AT for SAMPLE_MODE.

pre_existing_work: Matching ideas (brand gate, product-kind overlap, model-number conflicts, grounded quotes) were adapted from the author's Recall Sloth project (github.com/mikey92/recall-sloth, committed 21 Oct 2026). Code in this repository was written during the build window.
sample_mode: SAMPLE_MODE=true (or no Zetaris credentials) runs the same agents and SQL against an in-process DuckDB stand-in over the sample snapshots and synthetic CSVs; output is labelled SAMPLE and Zetaris is not used.
